with oil and the coming of the Spirit upon David.","Exodus 27:20–21 and Leviticus 24:1–4 describe pure oil continually sustaining the sanctuary lamps, commonly used typologically for continuing spiritual life and illumination.","Matthew 25:1–13, the parable of the ten virgins, is frequently interpreted in Christian teaching as contrasting possession of the Spirit or sustaining grace with an merely outward profession, although the passage itself does not identify the oil’s symbolism.","Revelation 4:5 identifies the seven burning lamps before God’s throne with the sevenfold Spirit of God, Spirit."],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Consecration, healing, joy, hospitality, or abundance, when oil appears outside a lamp context.","basis":["Exodus 30:22–33 and Leviticus 8:10–12 use oil for consecration.","Psalm 23:5 and Psalm 45:7 associate oil with honor and joy.","Mark 6:13 and James 5:14 associate oil with healing.","Deuteronomy 8:8 and Joel 2:24 present oil as a sign of agricultural abundance and blessing."],"prominence":"common"}],"has_settled_consensus":false,"confidence":"high","notes":"The Holy Spirit is the most recognizable symbolic identification of lamp oil Nevertheless, there is no settled cross-traditional consensus that lamp oil always carries that meaning. In particular, Matthew 25 never explicitly defines the oil, and many biblical scholars treat readiness as the parable’s point without assigning the oil a fixed allegorical referent."}
